note: Owner-editable (2026-09-25, extended 2026-09-26): how combat/reaction_triggers.py classifies a reaction's printed trigger text into one runnable kind. Trigger text is lowercased, a leading 'When' is dropped, then 'you can see/perceive/hear'/'you are aware of' clauses and a 'within N feet' clause are stripped out and recorded as filters (requires_sight, range_ft) before the remaining text is matched against the patterns below, in kind_order, first match wins. melee_only/ranged_only are set from the literal words 'melee'/'ranged' still present in the remaining text. Every attacked/hit/missed/damaged/save/drop_to_zero/bloodied/condition_gained pattern requires the literal word 'you' so a trigger about some other creature (an ally, a companion, a summon) never matches a self kind; ally_hit/ally_attacked/ally_missed/ally_damaged catch the 'an ally ... is hit/targeted/missed/damaged' phrasing instead (combat/typed_reactions.py offers these to other active Factory fighters on the target's own team). critical_hit/natural_1 match the clean 'a(n) (hostile) creature ... rolls a natural 1/20 on an attack roll' phrasing regardless of 'you', but the engine hook only ever runs them for an attack roll made against the reactor (owner 2026-09-26: on_attack_hit/on_attack_missed already have that context; a natural 1/20 rolled elsewhere -- an ability check, a saving throw, another creature's fight -- is not tracked, so those triggers still classify here for the owner's report but simply never find a matching attack to react to). technique_targets/technique_used are the 'a creature uses a technique that targets/within N feet of you' phrasing (combat/typed_executor.py's resolve_typed, non-weapon actions only). moved is classified for the report but stays non-runnable: no hook exists for a bystander reacting to someone else's movement. Anything left over (marks, terrain, stance, equipment, most multi-clause 'X, Y, or Z' triggers combining several of the events above, and other conditions the engine has no state for) is 'unsupported' and stays a GM call. 2026-09-26 step 8: moved is a willing move by another creature (hook after movement); forced_moved is kept apart (no hook yet); healed, any_drop_to_zero, creature_save_failed and creature_save_succeeded fire for any creature in range -- a harmful reaction only against a hostile creature, a helpful one only for you or an ally.

attacked: \ban attack roll(?: is made)? against you\b
critical_hit: \brolls? a natural 20 on an attack roll\b
natural_1: \brolls? a natural 1 on an attack roll\b
own_kill: (?:^|\b(?:when|after|whenever|if) )(?:it|the target|that creature|a creature you damaged|the marked creature) (?:drops|is reduced|falls) to 0\b

limits.note: Owner-editable (2026-09-26, 'make sure the mechanics aren't damaged'): checkable limits parsed out of a reaction's printed trigger alongside its kind, in combat/reaction_triggers.py. save_abilities matches a named ability immediately before 'saving throw' (a bare 'saving throw' or 'the selected saving throw' names none, so the row is unrestricted). damage_types matches any of these words anywhere in the trigger; used only by damaged/ally_damaged/drop_to_zero/bloodied rows -- the incoming damage type is unknown to a hit/attacked/missed row (no damage has been rolled yet), so it is never enforced there. conditions must stay the same set of words as the condition_gained pattern above (block_condition passes the lowercased condition name).

note_own: Owner 2026-09-26 ('we need the different resources to be generated'): own_hit / own_kill / own_save_failed are the character's own acts -- mostly a Sphere's or Foundation's resource generation -- run from typed_executor (block_attack, _deal, block_save) through typed_reactions.on_own_event. own_turn_start (auto/paths-b 2026-10-04, 'Immortal of Qi: at the start of each of your turns, regain 5 Qi' never fired) is the same seam for a printed trigger that is ONLY the reactor's own turn beginning: combat/typed_reactions.py's on_turn_start runs it, and a free (free: true) row costs no Reaction, which is how a printed resource generator ('regain', 'recover') on your own turn start runs. Its patterns are anchored at both ends on purpose: a turn-start moment that also names something the table cannot check (mounting, wielding an approved weapon, a prepared Counterstrike expiring, being Prone) still stays 'unsupported' and is the GM's, instead of firing every single turn.
